title: The gate suite entry point runs the same code path locally as in CI
asA: developer reproducing a CI failure on my own machine
iWant: the exact command the CI job ran to run the same way on my checkout
soThat: I reproduce the failure without guessing which flag or wrapper produced it

acceptanceCriteria.description: The CI provider's job step invokes the Node entry point with the same command a developer runs locally: the same file path, the same required arguments, the same environment variables the entry point reads (report directory path, tool-version pin). No CI-only wrapper script sits between the runner and the Node entry point. Template values the applying agent sets: The applying agent sets the elicited report directory; the AC substitutes the project's path for the illustrative default.
acceptanceCriteria.given: an rcf-lite project with this blueprint applied and a CI job wired per the illustrative example
acceptanceCriteria.when: a developer runs the same command line the CI job's invocation step records against their local checkout at the same commit
acceptanceCriteria.then: the aggregate report the local run writes at the configured report directory carries the same `runner.entryPoint`, the same `gates[]` ordering, and the same per-gate outcomes as the CI run's aggregate report for that commit, given the same rcf CLI version installed locally

acceptanceCriteria.description: The gate entry point reads no CI-provider-specific environment variable to alter its behaviour. Every configuration input the entry point honours is documented and available to a developer running locally. Template values the applying agent sets: The applying agent sets the elicited providerHint; the AC substitutes the project's provider assets for the illustrative GitHub-Actions asset set.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the applied blueprint's source path and the project's realised gate entry point
acceptanceCriteria.when: the reviewer greps the entry point's source and its dependency modules for reads against known CI-provider environment variables (`GITHUB_ACTIONS`, `GITLAB_CI`, `CIRCLECI`, `BUILDKITE`, `JENKINS_URL`)
acceptanceCriteria.then: no read of any of those variables gates the entry point's control flow or its gate set; if any such variable is read it is only for reporting into the aggregate report's `runner.environment` metadata field

acceptanceCriteria.description: A gate that produces different exit codes locally versus in CI (a stateful runner that reads process.env.CI) fails the parity assertion: the local invocation and the CI invocation must produce equal per-gate JSON reports (excluding wall-clock durations); a difference is flagged as a parity defect the operator resolves at the gate implementation, not by tolerating drift.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a gate whose exit code depends on process.env.CI (returns 0 locally, 1 in CI)
acceptanceCriteria.when: the same tree is run locally and under CI=1
acceptanceCriteria.then: the per-gate reports differ in verdict; the runner's parity-check flag (documented) marks the drift and the operator is directed to remove the CI-dependent branch from the gate
